items.evidence: From a stopped engine, in work/: `python catch.py run --seed 1 --ticks 600 --script '[{"tick":0,"input":"right"},{"tick":90,"input":"left"}]'` printed {"fall_speed": 4.2, "misses": 1, "over": false, "paddle_x": 0, "pieces": [{"x": 2.5, "y": 4.2967}, ...3 pieces], "score": 50, "tick": 600}: all of the brief's keys, tick = N.
`python catch.py frame --seed 1 --ticks 600 --script ... --out judge-scratch/f600.png` wrote a PNG; its IHDR reads 480 x 640. Same for 4 more frames.

Held left: paddle_x 4.367 (t1), 2.5 (t15), 0.5 (t30), 0 at t34, 35, 60, 100, 200. Held right: 4.633, 6.5, 8.5, then 9 at t34..200. A right/left/right/none zigzag over 500 ticks ended at 9; never outside 0..9.
Start 4.5; right 30 ticks -> 8.5; left 30 -> 0.5; left to 0 then right 30 ticks -> 4.0 (still 4.0 after holding none); left 30 then right 30 -> 4.5. 4 units per 30 ticks.

No input: 0 pieces at t0, 1 at t1 (x 2.5, y 15.5), still 1 at t72, 2 at t73 (new at y 15.5), 3 at t145. With a catching bot script, pieces on screen + score/10 + misses = ceil(t/72) at t=1000, 2017, 3000, 4321, 6000 (14, 29, 42, 61, 84). After the end, pieces unchanged for 5000 more ticks; they start again after restart (see s11).
Two runs seed 1, 800 ticks, same script printed identical JSON. First three columns at t145: seed 1 [2.5,0.5,3.5], seed 2 [11.5,0.5,7.5], seed 7 [10.5,3.5,8.5], seed 12345 [4.5,2.5,6.5].
Seed 1 held left: t218 score 0, piece x 2.5 at y 1.033 over paddle 0..3; t219 score 10, misses 0, that piece gone (4 -> 3 pieces); t220 score still 10, misses 0.
Seed 1 no input (paddle 4.5..7.5): t226 piece x 2.5 at y 0.5 (bottom at 0), misses 0; t227 misses 1, score 0, piece gone.
Seed 1 no input: t370 misses 2 over false; t371 misses 3 over true, score 0, 3 pieces; t372, t671, t5371 identical score/misses/pieces/paddle (also with right held from t381: paddle stays 4.5).

Bot script seed 1: t506 score 40, fall_speed 4, a piece fell 0.0667/tick; t507 score 50, fall_speed 4.2; from then on pieces fall 0.07/tick (5.7667 -> 5.6967 -> 5.6267). Later 4.41 at 10 catches, and 8.7315 = 4*1.05^16 at 82 catches.

Run (seed 1, right then left) over at t800 with score 50; restart at t800 -> t801 score 0, misses 0, over false, fall 4, one piece at x 2.5 y 15.5; t946 pieces [2.5,0.5,3.5] as in the first run's t146. No-input run restarted at t400: states at t401/402/545/546/771 match the first run's t1/2/145/146/371 exactly. A bot script shifted after a restart gave the same score 260 and pieces as unshifted.

Viewed f600.png, play2017.png, play_s3.png: HUD 'Score N  Misses left M' matching state; orange paddle at paddle_x*40 px (0, 360); red 40px squares where state says, e.g. state (11.5, 3.39) drawn at x 440-480, y ~484-524; (7.5, 9.37) at x 280-320, y ~245-285; (10.5, 15.5) at top, x 400-440.
Viewed over500.png (score 0) and over800.png (score 50): 'Game over', 'Final score 50' (resp. 0) and 'Press Enter to restart' in the middle, HUD 'Misses left 0'.

README.md 'How to play' gives keys Left/Right, A/D, Enter, rules and seed; 'The two checks' gives `python catch.py run ...` and `python catch.py frame ... --out out/frame.png`, run from work/, which worked as written from a stopped engine.

defects: After the end the frozen pieces stay drawn and can overlap the 'Game over' title and the HUD (seen in over800.png: a piece behind the 'G', another under 'Misses left'). Cosmetic, and the README says so.
Each check command starts and then stops the engine for the project unless --keep-engine is given, so it would stop an engine someone else had running for it.
catch.py writes a temporary .catch_args.json inside work/ on every call (it removes it afterwards).
Playing in a window (keys, Enter restart, 1/60 s stepping at the engine's tick rate) was not checked: no window was allowed. The builder says the same.

where.how: weighted_by_kind is exact (the run's own token counts times the weights); a step's kind is a reading of its command's text, and answered_tokens / written_tokens are characters / 4
